troubleshoot-a-java-based-business-appli.title: Troubleshoot a Java-based business application
prechecks: Determine scope by testing more than one approved client before treating the fault as application-server-wide.
Check the application/server logs for memory, connection-pool, dependency, class-loading or startup errors relevant to the incident window.
Check application server, database/dependency health and recent deployment/configuration changes before restarting components.
troubleshoot-a-java-based-business-appli.rollback: Record/export the current deployment and configuration. If a confirmed recent deployment/configuration caused the incident, use the application's approved deployment manager/change process to restore the previous known-good release/configuration and verify dependencies.
troubleshoot-a-java-based-business-appli.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Business application is not working".

troubleshoot-a-label-printer.title: Troubleshoot a label printer
prechecks: Check the printer's display for errors (out of labels, media mismatch).
Verify the printer's network connectivity (ping the IP).
Check the printer driver and ZPL/PCL command configuration.
troubleshoot-a-label-printer.rollback: If a driver update broke the printer, roll back to the previous driver version via Print Management.

troubleshoot-a-laptop-display-with-no-im.title: Troubleshoot a laptop display with no image
prechecks: Connect an external monitor to isolate internal display failure vs. GPU/video driver issue.
Check the display brightness and function keys (Fn+Fx).
Boot into BIOS/UEFI to confirm hardware POST completes.
troubleshoot-a-laptop-display-with-no-im.rollback: If a driver update broke the display, roll back the display driver via Device Manager. If the panel is physically damaged, initiate a hardware replacement ticket.
troubleshoot-a-laptop-display-with-no-im.symptom_match: "Windows device is not working correctly", "Display is not working".
troubleshoot-a-laptop-display-with-no-im.duplication: Related to #28 and #29 (external monitors) – but this is the internal display. Keep distinct.

troubleshoot-a-local-development-port-co.title: Troubleshoot a local development port conflict
prechecks: Run `netstat -ano` to identify the process using the conflicted port.
Check if the conflicting process can be stopped or reconfigured.
Verify the developer has administrative rights to stop the offending service.
troubleshoot-a-local-development-port-co.rollback: If you stop a critical process to free the port, restart it immediately after the conflicting application is re-configured.
troubleshoot-a-local-development-port-co.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Developer environment is not working".

troubleshoot-a-mobile-work-profile.title: Troubleshoot a mobile work profile
prechecks: Verify the device is enrolled in Intune/MDM and the work profile is provisioned.
Check the user's compliance status and app protection policies.
Confirm the work profile apps (Outlook, Teams) are up to date.
troubleshoot-a-mobile-work-profile.rollback: If the work profile becomes corrupted, remove and re-provision the profile via the Company Portal.
troubleshoot-a-mobile-work-profile.symptom_match: "Mobile device is not working", "Corporate access on a mobile device is not working".
troubleshoot-a-mobile-work-profile.duplication: Related to Batch B-2 #10 (mobile Outlook sync) and Batch B-3 #1 (iOS email config). Keep distinct for work profile-specific steps.

troubleshoot-a-pdf-that-will-not-open.title: Troubleshoot a PDF that will not open
prechecks: Try opening the PDF in a different reader (Edge, Chrome, Foxit) to isolate the application.
Check if the PDF is corrupted – attempt to open a known good PDF.
Verify the PDF reader is up to date.
troubleshoot-a-pdf-that-will-not-open.rollback: If a PDF reader update broke compatibility, roll back to the previous version via the application's installer or reinstall an older version.
troubleshoot-a-pdf-that-will-not-open.symptom_match: "File will not open", "Application is not working".
troubleshoot-a-pdf-that-will-not-open.duplication: Related to Batch B-3 #2 (broken file association) – but this is PDF-specific. Consider merging into a generic "File won't open" parent.
troubleshoot-a-pdf-that-will-not-open.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

troubleshoot-a-print-server-outage.title: Troubleshoot a print server outage
prechecks: Step 0: check print-server system/spool volume free space before clearing queues or restarting the Print Spooler.
Confirm whether the server itself is unreachable versus the Spooler, one queue, driver, port or downstream printer.
Check PrintService/System logs, Spooler dependencies and network/RPC reachability; preserve queued-job evidence before destructive cleanup.
troubleshoot-a-print-server-outage.rollback: Export/capture printer queues, ports and drivers before changes. Restore the previous approved print configuration if service worsens; do not mass-delete queued jobs without preserving required evidence and owner approval.
troubleshoot-a-print-server-outage.symptom_match: "A print server outage", "Printing or scanning is not working".
troubleshoot-a-print-server-outage.duplication: **Critical duplication detected.** This is a duplicate of Batch A, #17 ("Troubleshoot a print server outage") – that procedure was already audited and demoted to P1 in Batch A. Merge these two, keeping the Batch A version as the definitive parent.
troubleshoot-a-print-server-outage.final_verdict: Blocked until merged with Batch A #17.

troubleshoot-a-room-mailbox.title: Troubleshoot a room mailbox
prechecks: Check the room mailbox's calendar processing settings (auto-accept/decline).
Verify the room resource is not double-booked or overbooked.
Confirm the room's delegate/owner permissions.
troubleshoot-a-room-mailbox.rollback: If a calendar processing rule change broke booking, revert the rule to the previous state via Exchange Admin Center.
troubleshoot-a-room-mailbox.symptom_match: "Meeting room system is not working", "Exchange/M365 feature is not working".

troubleshoot-a-saml-application-error.title: Troubleshoot a SAML application error
prechecks: Step 0: check the identity-provider and application-provider service health before changing federation configuration.
Review sign-in/SAML diagnostic evidence for assertion, audience, recipient/ACS, issuer/entity-ID, clock-skew or signature/certificate errors.
Compare the Service Provider configuration with the authoritative IdP metadata, including certificate validity and endpoints.
troubleshoot-a-saml-application-error.rollback: Export/capture the working federation configuration before change. If a new federation configuration caused failure, restore the previous approved metadata/certificate/endpoints through the provider's supported administration process.
troubleshoot-a-saml-application-error.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Cannot sign in", "SAML authentication is failing".

troubleshoot-a-scanner-not-detected.title: Troubleshoot a scanner not detected
prechecks: Check the scanner's network connectivity (ping the IP) or USB connection.
Verify the scanner driver is installed and the TWAIN/WIA service is running.
Test the scanner from another computer to isolate the device vs. the workstation.
troubleshoot-a-scanner-not-detected.rollback: If a driver update broke scanning, roll back the driver via Device Manager.
troubleshoot-a-scanner-not-detected.symptom_match: "Scanning is not working", "Printing or scanning is not working".
troubleshoot-a-scanner-not-detected.duplication: Related to Batch B-2 #19 (scan to network folder) – that is the workflow, this is hardware detection. Keep distinct.

troubleshoot-a-service-account.title: Troubleshoot a service account
prechecks: Check whether the service identity is disabled, expired, locked or affected by password/secret/certificate expiry.
Check exact service/application authentication logs and all dependent services/tasks that use the identity before rotating credentials.
Review group/delegated permissions and confirm least privilege; identify whether the identity is a managed service account, vault-managed secret or traditional account.
troubleshoot-a-service-account.rollback: Do not roll back to an old secret merely because it is known. If credential rotation causes failure, restore service using the organisation's approved secret-management/rotation process, update all dependent consumers consistently, and revoke superseded credentials only after verification.
troubleshoot-a-service-account.symptom_match: "Access is denied or missing", "A server or infrastructure service is degraded".

troubleshoot-a-shared-mailbox.title: Troubleshoot a shared mailbox
prechecks: Verify the user has the correct permissions (Full Access, Send As, Send on Behalf).
Check if the shared mailbox is visible in Outlook or Outlook on the web.
Confirm the shared mailbox is licensed correctly (requires a license if it has >50GB data).
troubleshoot-a-shared-mailbox.rollback: If a permission change breaks access, revert the permissions immediately via Exchange Admin Center.
troubleshoot-a-shared-mailbox.symptom_match: "Access is denied or missing", "Exchange/M365 feature is not working".
troubleshoot-a-shared-mailbox.duplication: Related to Batch B-3 #6 (Grant shared mailbox access) – #6 is provisioning, #12 is troubleshooting. Keep distinct but cross-reference.

troubleshoot-a-stopped-windows-server-se.title: Troubleshoot a stopped Windows Server service
prechecks: Review System/Application/service-specific event logs for the stop/failure reason before restarting the service.
Check service dependencies and dependency health.
Check the service identity/credential, required permissions, resource capacity and recent configuration/update changes.
troubleshoot-a-stopped-windows-server-se.rollback: Capture the service configuration and recent change record. If a confirmed configuration/update caused the stop, revert only that approved change or restore the prior known-good service configuration; do not repeatedly restart a crashing service without diagnosis.
troubleshoot-a-stopped-windows-server-se.symptom_match: "A server or infrastructure service is degraded", "A Windows Server is unreachable" (indirect).

troubleshoot-a-usb-peripheral.title: Troubleshoot a USB peripheral
prechecks: Check Device Manager for driver errors (yellow exclamation mark).
Try the USB device on another computer to isolate device vs. workstation.
Test different USB ports and check USB root hub power.
troubleshoot-a-usb-peripheral.rollback: If a driver update broke the peripheral, roll back the driver via Device Manager. If a Windows Update caused it, uninstall the specific update.
troubleshoot-a-usb-peripheral.symptom_match: "USB device is not working", "Windows device is not working correctly".

troubleshoot-a-vdi-profile-issue.title: Troubleshoot a VDI profile issue
prechecks: Check broker/session health and profile-management logs for the exact user/session.
Check profile-store reachability, quota/disk capacity, locks and whether the issue follows the user across hosts.
Test an approved alternate host/pool to separate host, profile and user scope.
troubleshoot-a-vdi-profile-issue.rollback: Preserve the existing user profile before any reset. If a profile policy/configuration change caused regression, restore the previous policy; if a profile rebuild is required, retain the original until user data and settings are verified.
troubleshoot-a-vdi-profile-issue.symptom_match: "Cannot sign in", "VDI session is not working".

troubleshoot-a-webcam-on-windows.title: Troubleshoot a webcam on Windows
prechecks: Test the camera in the Windows Camera app to separate OS/hardware failure from Teams/application failure.
Check Windows camera privacy permissions and Device Manager status.
Check whether another process has exclusive camera use and test a known-good USB/internal camera path where applicable.
troubleshoot-a-webcam-on-windows.rollback: Record the existing driver/device settings. Restore the previous approved driver/configuration if an authorised driver change causes regression.
troubleshoot-a-webcam-on-windows.symptom_match: "Teams camera is not working", "Video/Camera is not working".
troubleshoot-a-webcam-on-windows.duplication: Duplicate of Batch B-2 #23 ("Troubleshoot Teams camera"). Merge these two – #16 is the generic Windows webcam procedure, #23 is the Teams-specific branch. The Teams procedure should call this one for hardware diagnostics.
troubleshoot-a-webcam-on-windows.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

troubleshoot-a-windows-certificate-servi.title: Troubleshoot a Windows certificate service request
prechecks: Check Certificate Authority and enrollment-service health before changing the requestor/client.
Verify certificate template publication, enrollment permissions and intended EKU/subject requirements.
Confirm time synchronization, trust chain and whether auto-enrollment/NDES/SCEP/web enrollment dependencies are healthy where applicable.
troubleshoot-a-windows-certificate-servi.rollback: Preserve the prior valid certificate until the replacement is verified where possible. If an incorrectly issued certificate causes failure, revoke it through the CA according to policy and reissue a valid certificate; do not export/reuse private keys as a rollback shortcut.
troubleshoot-a-windows-certificate-servi.symptom_match: "Cannot sign in", "A security or compliance concern is reported".

troubleshoot-a-windows-device-that-will-.title: Troubleshoot a Windows device that will not power on
prechecks: Check known-good power adapter/cable/dock and battery/charging indicators before opening hardware.
Disconnect nonessential peripherals and perform the vendor-approved power reset.
Check POST/diagnostic LED/beep codes and stop for battery swelling, liquid, overheating, smoke or electrical damage.
troubleshoot-a-windows-device-that-will-.rollback: Hardware power diagnosis generally has no software rollback. If a firmware/BIOS update is confirmed causal, use only the vendor-supported recovery mechanism; otherwise route to authorised hardware repair/replacement.
troubleshoot-a-windows-device-that-will-.symptom_match: "Windows device is not working correctly", "Device will not power on".

troubleshoot-a-windows-update-failure.title: Troubleshoot a Windows Update failure
prechecks: Check free disk space and the exact Windows Update error code before clearing update components.
Confirm the device can reach the organisation's configured update source (Windows Update for Business/WSUS/management service).
Review Windows Update/Event logs and update history for the failed KB/build and recent servicing-stack/reboot state.
troubleshoot-a-windows-update-failure.rollback: If an installed update is confirmed to cause regression, use the organisation's supported uninstall/known-issue rollback or recovery process. Preserve user data and record the KB/build; do not remove security updates without change/security approval.
troubleshoot-a-windows-update-failure.symptom_match: "Windows Update is failing", "Windows device is not working correctly".

troubleshoot-adobe-acrobat-sign-in.title: Troubleshoot Adobe Acrobat sign-in
prechecks: Check Adobe service/admin-console health and the user's licence/entitlement.
Check the configured identity provider/service health before clearing local credentials.
Compare browser/web authentication with the Acrobat client and inspect the exact federation/client error before cache reset.
troubleshoot-adobe-acrobat-sign-in.rollback: Capture federation/client configuration before change. If an approved SSO/federation configuration change causes regression, restore the previous provider configuration; do not restore expired or compromised credentials.
troubleshoot-adobe-acrobat-sign-in.duplication: Related to #9 (SAML application error) – this is the Acrobat-specific branch.

troubleshoot-an-application-that-will-no.title: Troubleshoot an application that will not install
prechecks: Check disk space and system requirements.
Verify the user has administrative rights to install.
Check for conflicting software (old versions, antivirus blocking).
troubleshoot-an-application-that-will-no.rollback: If a previously working app was broken by the installation, uninstall the new app via Control Panel and restore the previous version from backup or endpoint management.
troubleshoot-an-application-that-will-no.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Software install is failing".

troubleshoot-an-application-timeout.title: Troubleshoot an application timeout
prechecks: Determine single-user versus multi-user scope from multiple clients/locations.
Check application and database/server resource health, dependency latency and connection/thread-pool exhaustion.
Measure network latency/loss and correlate with the timeout timestamps before changing QoS or application settings.
troubleshoot-an-application-timeout.rollback: Capture the deployment/configuration/network policy before change. Revert the confirmed causal application/configuration/QoS change through the approved change process if timeouts worsen.
troubleshoot-an-application-timeout.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Application is slow or unresponsive".

troubleshoot-an-aws-ec2-instance-that-is.title: Troubleshoot an AWS EC2 instance that is unreachable
prechecks: Step 0: check AWS Health / service events for the affected account/region before changing the instance or network.
Check instance state plus EC2 system/instance status checks and recent events.
Check security groups, subnet route tables, NACLs and the intended management path before changing guest networking.
troubleshoot-an-aws-ec2-instance-that-is.rollback: Record security-group, route and NACL state before change. If a network-policy change causes lockout, restore the prior approved cloud-network configuration directly through AWS/IaC/control-plane access. Use Systems Manager only when it is already configured and reachable; do not assume it bypasses network controls.
troubleshoot-an-aws-ec2-instance-that-is.symptom_match: "A cloud or virtual resource is degraded", "A Windows Server that is unreachable" (if Windows).
troubleshoot-an-aws-ec2-instance-that-is.duplication: Unique. Keep distinct from Azure VM (#24) for provider-specific steps.

troubleshoot-an-azure-virtual-machine-th.title: Troubleshoot an Azure virtual machine that is unreachable
prechecks: Step 0: check Azure Service Health/resource health for the affected region/subscription before changing the VM or network.
Check VM power/provisioning state, Resource Health and Boot Diagnostics.
Check NSG, route, firewall and NIC configuration plus the intended management path before guest-OS changes.
troubleshoot-an-azure-virtual-machine-th.rollback: Export/capture NSG, route and VM/network configuration before change. If an Azure network-policy change causes lockout, restore the previous approved configuration through Azure control-plane/IaC access; use Serial Console/Boot Diagnostics for guest-OS diagnosis, not as a substitute for restoring an incorrect NSG.
troubleshoot-an-azure-virtual-machine-th.symptom_match: "A cloud or virtual resource is degraded", "A Windows Server that is unreachable" (if Windows).
troubleshoot-an-azure-virtual-machine-th.duplication: Unique. Keep distinct from AWS EC2 (#23) for provider-specific steps.

troubleshoot-an-electronic-signature-wor.title: Troubleshoot an electronic-signature workflow
prechecks: Check the e-signature provider's official service health before modifying templates/workflows.
Verify user entitlement/role, envelope/document state and recipient identity/status.
Review the workflow/audit trail for the exact failed step, timestamp and provider error before retrying or voiding.
troubleshoot-an-electronic-signature-wor.rollback: Version/capture workflow/template configuration before changes. Restore the previous approved template/workflow if a change caused failure. Void an erroneously sent envelope only under the authorised business/legal process; do not delete its audit trail.
troubleshoot-an-electronic-signature-wor.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Business workflow is not working".

troubleshoot-an-erp-client.title: Troubleshoot an ERP client
prechecks: Determine whether the problem is client-specific or affects multiple users/sites.
Check ERP application/server/database dependency health and relevant connection/session limits.
Verify user role/authorisation and recent client/server changes before reinstalling the client.
troubleshoot-an-erp-client.rollback: Record the current supported ERP client/configuration. If a confirmed client patch/configuration change caused failure, deploy the previous approved version/configuration through the enterprise software/ERP management process.
troubleshoot-an-erp-client.symptom_match: "Application is not accessible", "Business application is not working".

troubleshoot-an-external-display-on-maco.title: Troubleshoot an external display on macOS
prechecks: Check monitor power/input selection, cable/adapter/dock and physical connection using a known-good compatible path.
Determine whether the fault follows the monitor/cable/dock or the endpoint, and whether it occurs before sign-in/OS where testable.
Use the platform branch: Windows display/driver settings or macOS Displays/system information, without assuming an OS update rollback is available.
troubleshoot-an-external-display-on-maco.rollback: Record display/driver/dock configuration before changes. Restore the previous approved driver/display configuration if a change causes regression; replace faulty cable/adapter/dock/monitor through hardware support rather than attempting unsupported OS rollback.
troubleshoot-an-external-display-on-maco.symptom_match: "Apple macOS device is not working correctly", "Display is not working".
troubleshoot-an-external-display-on-maco.duplication: **Duplicate of #28 and #29 (external monitor issues).** Merge these three into one definitive "Troubleshoot an external monitor" procedure.

troubleshoot-an-external-monitor.title: Troubleshoot an external monitor
prechecks: Check monitor power/input selection, cable/adapter/dock and physical connection using a known-good compatible path.
Determine whether the fault follows the monitor/cable/dock or the endpoint, and whether it occurs before sign-in/OS where testable.
Use the platform branch: Windows display/driver settings or macOS Displays/system information, without assuming an OS update rollback is available.
troubleshoot-an-external-monitor.rollback: Record display/driver/dock configuration before changes. Restore the previous approved driver/display configuration if a change causes regression; replace faulty cable/adapter/dock/monitor through hardware support rather than attempting unsupported OS rollback.
troubleshoot-an-external-monitor.duplication: **Duplicate of #27 and #29.** Merge into one definitive procedure.

troubleshoot-an-external-monitor-with-no.title: Troubleshoot an external monitor with no signal
prechecks: Check monitor power/input selection, cable/adapter/dock and physical connection using a known-good compatible path.
Determine whether the fault follows the monitor/cable/dock or the endpoint, and whether it occurs before sign-in/OS where testable.
Use the platform branch: Windows display/driver settings or macOS Displays/system information, without assuming an OS update rollback is available.
troubleshoot-an-external-monitor-with-no.rollback: Record display/driver/dock configuration before changes. Restore the previous approved driver/display configuration if a change causes regression; replace faulty cable/adapter/dock/monitor through hardware support rather than attempting unsupported OS rollback.
troubleshoot-an-external-monitor-with-no.duplication: **Duplicate of #27 and #28.** Merge into one definitive procedure.

troubleshoot-an-http-403-error.title: Troubleshoot an HTTP 403 error
prechecks: Determine scope with another authorised user/client and capture the exact URL, identity, timestamp and 403 substatus/error detail.
Check reverse proxy/web/WAF/IIS or application logs to identify the layer returning 403.
Review identity/group membership and the relevant application/web/NTFS/ACL policy before granting additional access.
troubleshoot-an-http-403-error.rollback: Export/capture the relevant ACL/web/application configuration before change. If an authorised permission/configuration change broadens access or worsens the fault, restore the previous approved ACL/configuration immediately and verify least privilege.
